summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR18.4 billion, but order intake fell 30% to INR11.4 billion and gross margin slipped to 41.3%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 38% YoY to INR18.4 billion and PBT rose to INR4.9 billion, with EBITDA margin at 25.1%, within the mid-20s guided band. Order intake fell 30% YoY to INR11.4 billion, mainly on weak TBCB realisations in Jan-Mar 2026, so backlog eased 2.5% QoQ to INR209.3 billion. Gross margin fell to 41.3% from 45.3% in FY26, which management attributed to lower export mix, lower execution savings on elevated commodity prices, and HV business ramp-up. Two large related-party (RPT) orders, INR3,000 crore and INR1,300 crore, were delayed or on hold, and the company still has no firm plan for surplus cash of about INR16 billion beyond announced uses.

financial_highlights.change: -2.5% QoQ from INR214.6 billion at March 2026
vs 48.4% a year ago and 47% in Q4 FY26; FY26 full year 45.3%

financial_highlights.metric: Total available cash incl. cash pool lending

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export orders about INR5.2 billion of the INR11.4 billion Q1 intake; management says 80-90% of export orders come from GE Vernova group entities. Exports are 10-15% of backlog.

segments.name: Domestic TBCB and grid
segments.commentary: Third-party orders about INR6.5 billion in Q1, per management. Private customers are 77% of backlog, central utilities and PSUs 21%, state utilities 2%.

segments.name: HVDC
segments.commentary: Backlog is back-ended; meaningful growth expected from FY29 onward. Developers' first-phase bids for the next HVDC projects are expected to be decided in August or September 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at mid-20s.
Management stated it remains confident of the INR7,000-8,000 crore annual base order flow guidance, although Q1 base orders were about INR1,100 crore.
Domestic TBCB market expected flat or up 6-7% in FY27; double-digit growth not expected.
Backlog about 3.5x FY26 revenue; growth to be non-linear, with healthy growth in FY27 and FY28 and a step-up from FY29 on HVDC.
INR10 billion capacity expansion already announced; INR2.5 billion dividend planned in Q2 subject to shareholder approval; about INR16 billion of surplus cash with no firm allocation.
Chinese GIS suppliers recently approved for Indian market; impact on pricing and orders unclear until private TBCB negotiations start.
capex_capacity: INR10 billion capacity expansion programme announced in FY26, mostly inside existing plants on land already owned.
Vallam project (INR55 crore): part of capacity expected in Q1 CY27, balance by end-2027 (management said 'Q1 of 27' and 'end of 27'), against an earlier December 2026 target.
Capex on existing plants said to be tracking on schedule; management says it will not affect capacity utilisation.
Utilisation: some factories heavily loaded, others have room to grow.
demand_pricing: Q1 order intake down 30% YoY on weak TBCB realisations in Jan-Mar 2026; management says June-July TBCB pipeline is better, but the timing of conversion into orders is uncertain.

INR3,000 crore RPT order (a transformer project in the US per the call, though Q&A is unclear on the location) is on hold at the customer; approval lapses at the September AGM and would need re-validation. Management said it is not lost.
INR1,300 crore US data-centre RPT order not booked; expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27 after location and state change.
Data-centre orders are not significant in the current book; larger high-voltage data-centre projects are under discussion.

Commodity pass-through: transformers and HVDC carry IEEMA-linked escalation formulas; other turnkey work (CRGO and similar) is priced on forecast commodity costs with an 18-24 month order-to-execution lag.
Competition: Chinese GIS players approved; Tier-2 competition is limited in GIS and circuit breakers but present in other products.

qa_highlights.question: Are the INR3,000 crore and INR1,300 crore RPT orders being booked, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: None of the INR1,300 crore order is booked; it is expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27. The INR3,000 crore project is on hold at the customer over budget issues and would need fresh shareholder approval after the September AGM. Management said both are not lost.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a jump in export orders, and what is the RPT pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Export pipeline improved on US utility demand for instrument transformers and 400 kV GIS opportunities. Management declined to comment on the new RPT pipeline beyond saying it will go to shareholders when projects become live.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin bridge from 45.3% FY26 gross margin to 41.3% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: About 2-2.5 points from ramp-up of lower-margin HV business (offset at EBITDA level); 1-1.5 points from lower export share and a high-margin export order in FY26; and the rest from lower execution savings due to elevated commodity prices. EBITDA was 25.1%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the mid-20s EBITDA guidance intact, and how are commodity costs passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Mid-20s EBITDA guidance for FY27 is maintained. Transformers have formula-based escalation; other turnkey work relies on forecast costs, so cost pressure shows up in execution 1-2 years out.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Power Grid TBCB timeline stretching to 24-30 months a problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not affect capacity utilisation; ordering cycles may lengthen by about 3-4 months for longer tenders.

qa_highlights.question: What will the company do with surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said options are under evaluation and nothing is firm; announced uses are INR10 billion capex and INR2.5 billion dividend, leaving about INR16 billion unallocated.

risks_watch: Order intake: Q1 down 30% YoY; FY27 base order flow target of INR7,000-8,000 crore needs a sharp pick-up from Q1 run-rate of about INR1,100 crore.
Gross margin: 41.3% in Q1 vs 45.3% FY26; commodity cost pressure lags into execution over 18-24 months.
RPT timing: INR3,000 crore project on hold and needs re-approval after the September AGM; INR1,300 crore US data-centre order not yet booked.
HVDC pipeline slippage (South Kalamb and others) and back-ended execution until FY29.
Chinese GIS suppliers entering the Indian market may pressure pricing and share, especially in private TBCB.
Surplus cash of about INR16 billion is unallocated; capital allocation decision still pending.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the margin band, but cautious on order timing. Management was evasive on RPT pipeline, the HVDC pipeline, and capital allocation, offering no numbers beyond the announced items. Margin explanations were detailed and repeated when asked.
key_quotes: I will characterize this as a healthy number given the pace at which we are converting that backlog into revenue.
So we maintain our guidance of mid-20s EBITDA for the year. There is no reason that we should deviate from that right now.
Both of them are not lost.

growth.why: Management maintained mid-20s FY27 EBITDA margin guidance and expects domestic TBCB market flat to +6-7%, with healthy FY27-28 growth backed by ~INR209bn backlog (about 3.5x FY26 revenue) and an INR10bn capacity expansion, but Q1 order intake fell 30% and two large RPT orders (INR3,000cr on hold, INR1,300cr not booked) weaken near-term visibility.
